main_body: Two-storey half-timbered building with a hip tile roof, a plaster upper floor, a cobblestone ground floor, a door, windows and a hanging sign.
top_band: Roof slope: orange/amber tile rows from about row 4 to row 43 (x=48), with a highlighted ridge at the top. The scan shows alternating tile rows of L~140 and L~80. A dark eave line at rows 44-45 (L=15) separates it from the wall.
evidence: The large tiled roof slope reads clearly as a surface seen from above, and the hip slopes at left and right are shown as sloped planes. Below it sits the vertical south wall (rows 46-106). The eave edge is a dark line at rows 44-45 and shades the wall. The windows have dark inset frames, the flower boxes project, and the door has a dark frame. This construction matches the reference houses (house-h101_0 and house-h112_0-stone), which are correct 3/4 pieces. The roof slopes are visible and not a flat band.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have per-tile highlights across about 5-6 tones. The plaster is speckled and the cobbles are shaded one by one. Outlines lean brown or plum, and only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral. The candidate has 19 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 191 distinct colours against 185 and 66, and 0% flat fill. It is as rich as the references and not sticker-like.
